content.user_title: Convert Japanese Era and Gregorian Dates
content.value_statement: Japanese era dates can be confusing when an era changes during a calendar year. This skill applies daily boundaries and arithmetic to convert dates offline.
actual_capabilities: Convert Gregorian dates into Reiwa, Heisei, Showa, Taisho, or Meiji dates within the supplied boundaries.
Convert Japanese era years into Gregorian years using the documented arithmetic formula.
Distinguish dates on opposite sides of an era transition within the same Gregorian year.
Use gannen notation for the first year of an era.
Identify dates outside the supplied range and reject dates beyond an era boundary.
Flag the Gregorian basis when interpreting Meiji dates before Japan adopted the Gregorian calendar.
limitations: Dates before October 23, 1868, are outside the supplied conversion table.
Historical lunisolar dates are not converted; all date boundaries use the Gregorian calendar.
Future era changes require a table update and cannot be predicted.
Holiday and rokuyo calculations require separate skills; the referenced shared response checklist is not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Prepare Japanese forms
use_cases.description: Convert a Gregorian birth date into Japanese era notation and show both formats for comparison.

use_cases.title: Interpret historical dates
use_cases.description: Translate supported era dates into Gregorian dates while noting calendar limitations for early Meiji records.

use_cases.title: Check transition examples
use_cases.description: Compare dates around the Showa, Heisei, and Reiwa transitions to prepare expected results for calendar tests.

prompt_templates.title: Convert one Gregorian date
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert September 11, 2026, into Japanese era notation. Show both Gregorian and Japanese era dates.

prompt_templates.title: Convert an era year
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert Heisei 7 into a Gregorian year. Explain the arithmetic and do not invent a month or day.

prompt_templates.title: Compare an era transition
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert April 30 and May 1, 2019, into Japanese era dates. Explain the boundary and first-year notation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare adjacent dates across an era change.

prompt_templates.title: Review mixed historical inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review Showa 64 June, October 22, 1868, and January 1, 1872. Flag invalid or unsupported inputs and explain historical calendar caveats.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: separate invalid dates, unsupported dates, and Gregorian-based historical conversions.

output_examples.input: Convert September 11, 2026, into Japanese era notation.

output: Heisei began on January 8; gannen denotes its first year.

output_examples.input: Convert Showa 64 June into a Gregorian date.
output: This Japanese era date does not exist.
Showa ended on January 7, 1989, so Showa 64 has no June.
The input is not rounded to a nearby valid date.

best_practices: Provide the month and day when converting a Gregorian year that contains an era transition.
Display Gregorian and Japanese era dates together to reduce transcription errors.
State the Gregorian basis for early Meiji dates and check historical records for lunisolar notation.
anti_patterns: Assigning one era to every date in a Gregorian transition year.
Rounding impossible era dates into nearby valid dates.
Guessing dates before the supported range or predicting future era names.

faq.question: Does conversion require internet access?
faq.answer: No. Conversion uses the supplied era table and arithmetic; the URLs are reference citations.

faq.question: Which Japanese eras are supported?
faq.answer: The table covers Meiji, Taisho, Showa, Heisei, and Reiwa, starting on October 23, 1868.

faq.question: What does gannen mean?
faq.answer: Gannen means the first year of an era. The skill recommends this notation instead of writing year 1.

faq.question: Can I provide only a Gregorian year?
faq.answer: Yes, but transition years can contain two eras. Provide the month and day to identify the correct era.

faq.question: Does this convert historical lunisolar dates?
faq.answer: No. It uses Gregorian dates and warns that early Meiji records may use the historical lunisolar calendar.

faq.question: What happens with invalid dates or future era changes?
faq.answer: Impossible era dates are rejected rather than rounded. Future era changes require updating the table after an official announcement.
